title: Self-host check: base branch from the main checkout, one git call when nothing moved
lead: The "daemon behind main" check compares the running build with the branch the main checkout is on (what landing already uses) instead of a hard-coded `refs/heads/main`, and makes one git call per snapshot or status read when that branch has not moved. The cost is measured first and reported.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
S114 and S109 later notes, re-read at HEAD (2026-10-31); owner decision, 2026-10-31: the base branch is the main checkout's current branch, as landing uses it.

- `projectBuild` (`internal/daemon/build.go:20-41`) runs `git cat-file -e REV^{commit}`, then `git rev-parse --verify refs/heads/main^{commit}`, then (when the two differ) `git merge-base --is-ancestor`: one to three git processes per project, on every `snapshot` (`internal/daemon/handlers.go:270`) and `status` (`:327`) call. It is not cached. The result depends only on the build revision (fixed for the life of the daemon), the project path and the tip of the base branch.
- `refs/heads/main` is hard-coded at `build.go:31` because the registry has no base-branch field (`internal/registry/registry.go` has none). Landing reads the base from the main checkout: `internal/engine/land.go:44-45` runs `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` in the project path and treats that as the base; `docs/design.md:397` says "The base branch is the branch the main checkout is on". The self-host check is the only reader that still says `main`.
- S109 later note (2026-10-26): the daemon calls `BoardRuns` uncached, about one extra `relay-run list` per second per client at the 1 s Runs interval. Not measured. This slice measures it (step 1) and does not change it.

Measure first (S131 spec): the numbers decide nothing about the fix below, which is small and correct on its own; they go into the handoff so the owner sees what the cost was and whether a deeper cache (reading the base tip from the cache's `Head` part, `internal/cache/cache.go:130`, so a hit makes no git call) is worth a later slice.

Behavior of the new check, for a daemon whose build revision exists in the project (`selfHost`, unchanged):
- One call, `git rev-parse HEAD --symbolic-full-name HEAD` in the project path, gives the tip and the ref (`refs/heads/NAME`, or `HEAD` when detached; checked 2026-10-31 on a scratch repo: two lines, exit 0). A repository with no commit fails with exit 128.
- On a branch: behind means the build revision is an ancestor of the tip and differs from it. This is the old rule with the branch name taken from the checkout.
- Detached HEAD, no commit, or a failed read: not behind (as a missing `main` is today, `docs/design.md:1772`). `selfHost` is still computed.
- The result is cached per (project path, build id, tip, ref). A call whose key matches runs only the one `rev-parse`. A key that differs runs the full set once and replaces the entry.

The notice text stays `daemon behind main: restart with ork daemon restart` (`internal/daemon/build.go:16`), and the fields stay `self_host` and `behind_main`. The wording says "main" while the base may be another branch; renaming is a UI and docs change that nobody asked for, so it is left (see the manifest question).

Class: E (daemon paths are listed). Not a UI slice: no TUI code, golden view or CLI output changes; docs/dashboard.md gets one wording change in the self-hosting paragraph only.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `internal/daemon/build_test.go`, using `selfHostRepo(t)` and a counting wrapper for git: a script in `t.TempDir()` that appends its arguments to a log file and then `exec`s the real `git`, installed with `setGitBin(d, script)`.
- `TestProjectBuildCachedUntilHeadMoves`: for a repo on `main` and a build equal to its tip, two calls to `d.projectBuild` return the same result; the second makes exactly one git call (`rev-parse HEAD --symbolic-full-name HEAD`). After `git commit --allow-empty` on `main` the next call makes more than one call and now reports behind for a build that is the old tip; the call after that makes one call again. Fails first: every call runs the full set.
- `TestBaseBranchIsTheMainCheckoutsCurrentBranch`: with the checkout on a branch `trunk` that is one commit ahead of the build revision and `main` still at the build revision, `behind_main` is true (the old code compares with `main` and says false). With the checkout on `main` and `trunk` ahead, it is false. Fails first on the first assertion.
- `TestNoBaseBranchIsNotBehind`: detached HEAD (`git checkout --detach`) gives `self_host` true and `behind_main` false; a repository with no commit gives both false (the build commit cannot exist); a deleted `main` while the checkout is on another branch still compares with that branch.
- `TestSnapshotAndStatusAgreeAfterTheCacheHits`: `d.status` and `d.snapshot` report the same pair twice in a row (the existing `buildProject` helper already asserts the pair; keep it).
- Update `TestDaemonBehindBaseBranch`: its last two assertions pin the old rule ("worktree HEAD used instead of main" and "missing main reported behind"). Under the owner's rule the base is the checkout's branch, so after `git checkout -b slice` the last case (`git branch -D main` while on `slice`) is behind true for the original base commit; keep the "diverged build is not behind" and "equal revision is not behind" assertions, and move the "no base" case to the detached HEAD test above.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Tests first; see each fail for the stated reason.

1. Measure (report in the handoff, no code kept): write a small counting wrapper for `git` in `.scratch/` of the main checkout (not `/tmp`), point a test daemon at it through `GitBin`, and record the number of git processes and the wall time of one `snapshot` and one `status` call for a registered project at HEAD of this repo, before the change. Count the `relay-run list` calls of `BoardRuns` over ten seconds of a subscribed client with one active run. If a live daemon is not available to the implementer, say so and report the call count from a test with the fake slicer instead. State what you could and could not measure.
2. Replace `refs/heads/main` in `projectBuild` with the base read from the checkout, using the single call above, and keep the guards on `revision` (40 or 64 hex characters, `cat-file -e` success) exactly as they are. Treat exit 128 and detached `HEAD` as "no base".
3. Add the cache: a `map[string]buildEntry` on `Daemon` (key: path, build id, tip, ref joined with `\x00`; value: `selfHost`, `behind`), one mutex, bounded to the registered projects (drop entries for a project when its key changes; do not grow without limit). Compute on a miss exactly as today. Never cache a failed read.
4. Docs as listed, marked *proposed* where they describe behavior beyond the roadmap. Do not rename the notice, the wire fields or the `BehindNotice` constant.
5. `CHANGELOG.md`: one entry under `## Unreleased`, added last.
6. Do not touch `internal/engine/land.go` (it is the reference), `BoardRuns`, `internal/cache`, or `internal/registry`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/daemon`
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` (must print nothing)
- `slicer check`
- `adj lint`
- The handoff reports the measurement from Implement step 1 (processes and time per snapshot and per status call before and after, and the `BoardRuns` rate), or says why it could not.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Self-host check: base branch from the main checkout, cached by tip".
